findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes when TopicUser row does not exist
findings.body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb TopicsController#unsubscribe does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` then immediately calls `tu.notification_level`. If the user never visited/tracked the topic there is no TopicUser row, so `tu` is nil and the request raises NoMethodError and returns 500. Email recipients who never interacted are exactly the users most likely to click the new per-topic unsubscribe link, so this breaks the feature.

findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe via GET is CSRF-able
findings.body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb the new `unsubscribe` action mutates `TopicUser.notification_level` and saves, but config/routes.rb exposes it as `GET t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` and `GET t/:topic_id/unsubscribe`. Any logged-in user visiting an attacker page with `` or a crawler/prefetcher following the email link will silently mute/regularize the topic with no CSRF token or confirmation. Mutating actions must not be GET.

findings.title: Unsubscribe lacks visibility/authorization check
findings.body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb `unsubscribe` builds `TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user)` and then mutates notification state without `guardian.ensure_can_see!` and without rescuing `Discourse::InvalidAccess` the way `show` does. This lets a logged-in user probe private-message/secured-category topic IDs and change state on topics they cannot see, and turns forbidden topics into unhandled 500s instead of 403/404.

findings.title: Unsubscribe email template now requires unsubscribe_url and can break delivery
findings.body: In lib/email/message_builder.rb `body` and `html_part` unconditionally interpolate `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` when `add_unsubscribe_link` is true. After config/locales/server.en.yml changed `unsubscribe_link` to require `%{unsubscribe_url}`, any builder with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but no `unsubscribe_url` in opts raises `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` and fails the email. The builder is generic, `user_preferences_url` was always present but `unsubscribe_url` is only supplied by `send_notification_email`, so one missed caller breaks all delivery for that email.
